### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **11** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/metadata-core`, `@objectstack/metadata`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/plugin-sharing`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **347** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **34** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`, `packages/lint/src/validate-org-axis-red-lines.ts`, `packages/metadata-core/src/injected-system-columns.ts`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**106** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6390fe52cecd263f09225d0d6d9b74412d111a67`.

⛔ **18** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **34** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`, `packages/lint/src/validate-org-axis-red-lines.ts`, `packages/metadata-core/src/injected-system-columns.ts`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `isSystem (5 routes)`, `packageId (4 routes)`
- **5** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 72 pages)`, `objectName (symbol, 40 pages)`, `VALIDATION_FAILED (literal, 33 pages)`, `organization_id (literal, 38 pages)`, `/api/v1/meta (route, 42 pages)`
- **50** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **55** of **207** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **159** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6390fe52cecd263f09225d0d6d9b74412d111a67` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `0eabed0ff7c8f642de72a51d66523db5f813070a` — the merge of head `e45133760b7b95682a42b174a193d627ed5f996b` into base `6390fe52cecd263f09225d0d6d9b74412d111a67`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 0eabed0ff7c8f642de72a51d66523db5f813070a && git checkout 0eabed0ff7c8f642de72a51d66523db5f813070a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6390fe52cecd263f09225d0d6d9b74412d111a67 e45133760b7b95682a42b174a193d627ed5f996b && git checkout -B drift-repro 6390fe52cecd263f09225d0d6d9b74412d111a67 && git merge --no-ff e45133760b7b95682a42b174a193d627ed5f996b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6390fe52cecd263f09225d0d6d9b74412d111a67
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 6390fe52cecd263f09225d0d6d9b74412d111a67` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each judged against ADR-0142 (Accepted, main) and the runtime in this head. Check-runs on the head: 58 success, 5 skipped (the full-battery jobs that never run on a pull_request event), 0 red.

Judged RIGHT (declared and enforced in this PR):

- Metadata type `queue` and stack key `queues` (QueueSchema, registry entry code-only, loadOrder 16, BUILTIN_METADATA_TYPE_SCHEMAS binding, METADATA_ARRAY_KEYS, ARTIFACT_FIELD_TO_TYPE, PLURAL_TO_SINGULAR, META_URL, MAP_SUPPORTED_FIELDS, COMPOSE_KEY_DISPOSITIONS concat, SAME_STACK_ENTRY_IDENTITY last-wins-by-name). Read at runtime by OwnershipQueueService.resolveQueue registry-first, then sys_queue rows; a declared name switched off in the activation ledger resolves nowhere, not even to an authored row (D1 one namespace). Declared members positions-only by a z.literal (merge question 18). Activation door serves `queue` through declaredQueueNamed.
- Metadata type `assignment_rule` and stack key `assignmentRules`. Read on every insert by AssignmentRuleEvaluator after the beforeInsert hooks and the organization derivation, before the write, only for rows with owner_id and queue both empty; never refuses an insert; parks on an empty pool; unresolved target leaves the row ownerless with queue unset; least_loaded counts under the entry's `load` lowered by compileCelToFilter and never counts everything; round_robin advances sys_assignment_cursor under the `{ version }` precondition with bounded retries. Schema refinements (strategy only with a queue target, load required with least_loaded and refused otherwise, unique entry names, queue target by machine name) are in the Zod and listed in dropped-refinements.baseline.json as unprojected sites (a reading, not a defect: new refinements under the closed projection list).
- `ShareRecipientType` gains `queue` (D7): expandRecipient expands through the one expander; declared-rule translator maps it; defineRule and the Zod hold the value to a machine name; queue-hooks recompute on sys_queue / sys_queue_member / activation-ledger writes; recipient-membership-recompute looks through queues on a position or team write; the BU-tree recompute asks per queue rule whether a BU-kind member is present; sys_sharing_rule.recipient_type select gains the option; the lint red-line table re-decides `queue` as a flat kind; the runtime union and the authorable enum are now equal and the pin flips to equality.
- `queue` approver type re-admitted (D6): resolveApproverSpec gains the branch (expandMembers on the addressing purpose, empty expansion warns and contributes no slot, the literal queue:name slot is never written); `queue` leaves NON_AUTHORABLE_APPROVER_TYPES and so xEnumDeprecated; APPROVER_VALUE_BINDINGS.queue is the new `registry-and-record` kind (open item 1 delivered, published on the wire as `registry-and-data`); APPROVER_ORG_SCOPED.queue true and the service expands in directoryOrg; lint adds `queue` to GROUP_ROUTED_TYPES and the unsupported arm stops firing by construction (it reads the binding's source). The Console cell stays free text until the two-source picker (objectui lane) - declared as deferred, nothing advertises a picker.
- Injected `queue` column on exactly the owner tier (resolveInjectedSystemColumns.queue = owner; QUEUE_FIELD_DEF text, system, readonly false, hidden; injectedSystemColumnDefs; applySystemFields; metadata-core re-export; SYSTEM_FIELD_LABELS in four locales; display-name derivation skips the injected text column so a queue name is never a derived title). Author-declared `queue` on an eligible BASE layer refused at registerObject with 422 INVALID_METADATA (ObjectQueueColumnRefusedError) and semantic migration entry 18 carries the surface, replacement, reason and acceptance criteria. See the ① finding below on the extend layer.
- Claim, release, move, insert naming a queue (D3/D4) at step 3.5: the table in ownership-queue-gate.ts matches the ADR; claim is by-id only (resolveEngineUpdateDispatch), admitted on the sharing write verdict `allow` (reused from step 2.7 where asked, else asked once; both principals under delegation), and sets writePrecondition `{ owner_id: null }`; release needs a home queue and an unchanged queue; move and an explicit-empty-owner park need the transfer grant; a member's insert naming a queue stays an owned record with a home queue (merge question 13); guest refused on both anchors; QUEUE_NOT_FOUND 422 on a name that resolves nowhere, fail-closed with no service. The engine lowers the precondition to driver.updateMany over `{ ...expect, id }` and reads back; zero rows is 409 CONCURRENT_UPDATE; no updateMany degrades with one warn. The bare `{ owner_id: null }` map reaches the driver without the engine's where normalisation: on driver-sql the top-level loop admits a null comparand (only undefined is refused) and emits builder.where(column, null), which knex compiles as IS NULL, so the claim race is correct on SQL - judged right, but the only pins are a hand-written fake driver in objectql/ownership-queue.test.ts; no shipped driver is exercised under the precondition (a reading for the lane, not a refusal).
- Sitting-record access path (D3): buildReadFilter and the update arm of buildWriteFilter carry `owner_id IS NULL AND queue IN callerQueues`, the delete arm returns before it (verified on main), checkEdit tests sitsInCallersQueue ahead of the public-OWD abstain and apart from matchesOwnerScope; hasQueueColumn is provenance-based so an author's own field and a federated object get no disjunct; guest gets none; membership memoised per request context.

The sentences stay true; the provenance pointers go. A reading for the Tier H approver, not a contract defect.

Judged WRONG or incomplete:

- FINDING ①-1 (declared deviation that leaves the ADR's refusal half-enforced): the D3 registration refusal runs on base layers only (`ownership !== 'extend'` in registerObject), and foldExtendersOntoDefinition merges an extender through mergeObjectDefinitions as `{ ...base.fields, ...extension.fields }`. An `objectExtensions` entry declaring `fields.queue` on a user-owned object therefore replaces the injected QUEUE_FIELD_DEF silently: provenance of the served object reads `author`, hasQueueColumn and carriesQueueColumn go false, so the access path, the assignment seam and the sharing disjunct switch off while the gate (which tests field presence) keeps adjudicating the author's business column - the inert state ADR-0142 merge question 15 refuses for the base layer and ADR-0078 forbids. The audit family already has the precedent guard in the same fold (applyAuditFieldGovernance, the created_at case). The PR body names the base-layer limit as a deviation but neither closes the extension door nor files it. Fix in this PR (govern `queue` in the fold as the audit family is, or refuse it at the extension door with the same prescription), or file the card and narrow the migration entry's `surface` text, which today claims every registration door.

### ② Semver level

- The changeset .changeset/25769-ownership-queue.md grades every moved published package `minor` (spec, objectql, metadata-core, metadata, plugin-security, plugin-sharing, plugin-approvals, lint, runtime, platform-objects, app-shell, skills), declares `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, carries a BREAKING banner with the FROM-TO remedy, and the ADR-0087 marker `registered object-queue-field-reserved` matching the new semantic entry 18. Those declarations are RIGHT for this diff: an author-declared `queue` field on an `ownership: user` object was accepted on main and is refused on this head, so the kind is `narrowed` (several kinds - added types plus a refused name - resolve `narrowed` over `added`) and the arm is `(narrowing)`, BREAKING.
- FINDING ②-1 (the two carriers disagree, and the gate read the wrong one): the PR body declares `Clause-②: yes` and `Metadata-protocol: added`, the claim's copy from before commit 6f98217859be ("feat(spec)!: declare the reserved queue column as a narrowing") turned the changeset breaking. AGENTS.md requires both line-initial declarations in the PR body AND the changeset body, and the Check Changeset level axis reads the PR body (scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs readClause2Line / readMetadataProtocolLine over pr.body), so the green level-axis verdict graded a `yes` / `added` PR, not the `yes (narrowing)` / `narrowed` change the diff and the changeset carry; check-adr-0087-registration read the changeset's arm, so the two gates judged two different declarations. The body must read `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`. Everything derived from the arm was left unrederived too: the title carries no `!` while the changeset is `feat!:`; the body states "No full dogfood battery: the title has no `!` and Clause-② has no narrowing arm", which under os-dev's own rule (全量 dogfood owed when Clause-② carries a `(narrowing)` arm) is now an owed run the report says was not made; the body's "Tests and gates" section names head 578e7a417f73 and 168 files / +6230 / -380 where the head is 9ada3a92 with 184 files / +6353 / -397. Dogfood shards never run on a pull_request event (ci.yml two speeds), so the check-runs cannot stand in for that battery.
